paragraphs.title: Keeping the Laws in the Land

easy.question: What must the Israelites keep and do in the land?
answers: The statutes and judgments
The customs of the nations
The names of the idols
easy.explanation: The verse says that the Israelites must observe and do the statutes and judgments.

easy.question: Where did the nations worship their gods?
answers: Only inside their homes
On the high mountains, hills, and under every green tree
Only near rivers
easy.explanation: The verse specifically mentions the high mountains, hills, and every green tree.

easy.question: What were the Israelites commanded to do to the nations’ altars and images?
answers: Preserve them
Decorate them
Tear them down and cut them down
easy.explanation: They were commanded to overthrow the altars and cut down the graven images.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites commanded to destroy the nations’ worship sites?
answers: To turn them into marketplaces
To remove idolatry from the land
To mark the borders of the land
medium.explanation: Destroying the altars, pillars, and images was intended to remove idolatry from the land.

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: Receiving the land, destroying the nations’ worship sites, and keeping the Lord’s laws
Destroying the worship sites, leaving the land, and receiving laws
Keeping the nations’ laws, building images, and receiving the land
medium.explanation: The passage first speaks of the land given to Israel, then the destruction of pagan worship, and finally keeping the Lord’s laws.

medium.question: In the verse phrase “break their pillars,” what are “pillars”?
answers: Law books
Sacred trees
Stone pillars set up for idol worship
medium.explanation: The context of altars and graven images shows that these were stone pillars used in pagan worship.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between destroying pagan worship sites and “Ye shall not do so unto the Lord”?
answers: Every place of prayer must be destroyed
Pagan worship must be distinguished from worship of the Lord
All gods may be worshiped
challenge.explanation: The verses command the destruction of pagan symbols but stress that the Lord must not be treated in the same way.

challenge.question: What does “all the days that ye live upon the earth” teach about keeping the laws?
answers: The duty continues throughout Israel’s life in the land
The laws were required only on the day they entered the land
The laws were intended only for leaders
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes an ongoing obligation, not a one-time act.

challenge.question: What does the repeated command “utterly destroy” emphasize?
answers: Destroying only one site
Leaving some of the images behind
Completely destroying the places of idolatrous worship
challenge.explanation: The repetition strengthens the command and emphasizes complete destruction.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the contrast between destroying pagan worship sites and “Ye shall not do so unto the Lord”?
answers: Every place of prayer must be destroyed
Pagan worship must be distinguished from worship of the Lord
All gods may be worshiped
questions.explanation: The verses command the destruction of pagan symbols but stress that the Lord must not be treated in the same way.

questions.question: What does “all the days that ye live upon the earth” teach about keeping the laws?
answers: The duty continues throughout Israel’s life in the land
The laws were required only on the day they entered the land
The laws were intended only for leaders
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes an ongoing obligation, not a one-time act.

questions.question: What does the repeated command “utterly destroy” emphasize?
answers: Destroying only one site
Leaving some of the images behind
Completely destroying the places of idolatrous worship
questions.explanation: The repetition strengthens the command and emphasizes complete destruction.

paragraphs.title: The Chosen Place and Joy in Worship

easy.question: Where were the Israelites commanded to go?
answers: To the place the Lord would choose
To the place nearest their homes
To a place chosen by the tribes
easy.explanation: The verse commands them to go to the place the Lord would choose from among all the tribes.

easy.question: What would the Israelites bring to the chosen place?
answers: Only fruit
Offerings, tithes, and gifts
Only clothing
easy.explanation: The passage lists burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, heave offerings, vows, and freewill offerings.

easy.question: What would the Israelites celebrate at the chosen place?
answers: All the work of their hands
Their wars
Only their homes
easy.explanation: The verse says, “Ye shall rejoice in all that ye put your hand unto.”

medium.question: What sequence is described in these verses?
answers: They come to the place, bring gifts, eat, and rejoice
They eat, go to war, and then bring tithes
They choose a king, build houses, and then come to the place
medium.explanation: They first come to the place the Lord chooses, bring their offerings, and then eat and rejoice there.

medium.question: What is the connection between the Lord’s blessing and rejoicing in verse 7?
answers: Joy comes because the Lord has blessed their work
Joy comes because no work is required
Joy comes because everyone chose a place for himself
medium.explanation: The verse says they will rejoice in all the work of their hands, which the Lord has blessed.

medium.question: In “His habitation,” what does “habitation” mean?
answers: A place where He commands
A place where He dwells and is present
A place from which He travels
medium.explanation: The verse describes the place where the Lord causes His name to dwell—His appointed place of presence.

challenge.question: Why is it emphasized that the place would be chosen “out of all your tribes”?
answers: So each tribe would worship in a different place
To emphasize that the place is for all Israel, not one tribe alone
So each tribe could choose its own sanctuary
challenge.explanation: The phrase emphasizes one central place chosen from among all the tribes, rather than a private tribal site.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “ye and your households”?
answers: Worship and joy include the family, not only the individual
Only heads of families may eat
The households must remain in their former location
challenge.explanation: The verse includes the households in the rejoicing, showing that worship and celebration involve the family.

challenge.question: Which phrase shows that the joy is also connected with work and daily livelihood?
answers: “Out of all your tribes”
“Before the Lord your God”
“In all that ye put your hand unto”
challenge.explanation: The phrase refers to people’s work and activities, including the blessing of their livelihood.

questions.question: Why is it emphasized that the place would be chosen “out of all your tribes”?
answers: So each tribe would worship in a different place
To emphasize that the place is for all Israel, not one tribe alone
So each tribe could choose its own sanctuary
questions.explanation: The phrase emphasizes one central place chosen from among all the tribes, rather than a private tribal site.

questions.question: What can be inferred from the phrase “ye and your households”?
answers: Worship and joy include the family, not only the individual
Only heads of families may eat
The households must remain in their former location
questions.explanation: The verse includes the households in the rejoicing, showing that worship and celebration involve the family.

questions.question: Which phrase shows that the joy is also connected with work and daily livelihood?
answers: “Out of all your tribes”
“Before the Lord your God”
“In all that ye put your hand unto”
questions.explanation: The phrase refers to people’s work and activities, including the blessing of their livelihood.

easy.question: How is the people’s behavior described “here this day”?
answers: Everyone does whatever is right in his own eyes
Everyone worships only at the temple
Everyone does exactly the same thing
easy.explanation: The verse says that every person does whatever is right in his own eyes.

easy.question: What would the Israelites bring to the place the Lord chose?
answers: Only the tithes
Everything the Lord commanded, including offerings and gifts
Only the firstfruits
easy.explanation: The passage mentions burnt offerings, sacrifices, tithes, heave offerings, and vows.

easy.question: Who would join in rejoicing before the Lord?
answers: Only the priests
Only the tribal leaders
The family, servants, and the Levite
easy.explanation: The passage includes sons, daughters, menservants, maidservants, the Levite, and the household.

medium.question: What would happen before the Israelites brought their offerings to the place the Lord chose?
answers: They would cross the Jordan, settle in the land, and receive rest from their enemies
They would return to the wilderness
They would choose a separate place for each offering
medium.explanation: The verses describe crossing the Jordan, settling in the land, and receiving rest from their enemies before establishing the chosen place.

medium.question: In “the land which the Lord your God giveth you to inherit,” what does “inherit” mean?
answers: Hides from you
Gives to you as a possession
Takes away from you
medium.explanation: The context describes the land that the Lord gives Israel as a possession.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites commanded to include the Levite in their joy and meals?
answers: Because the Levite was a king
Because the Levite did not live in the land
Because the Levite had no portion or inheritance with Israel
medium.explanation: The verse explicitly says that the Levite had no portion or inheritance with Israel.

challenge.question: What is the central change between the situation “this day” and the future in the land?
answers: Instead of everyone doing as he pleases, worship will take place where the Lord chooses
Instead of worshiping the Lord, they will worship idols
Instead of rejoicing, the people will be forbidden to rejoice
challenge.explanation: The present situation involves individual choice, while the future commands offerings at the place chosen by the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “the place which the Lord shall choose in one of thy tribes”?
answers: Each tribe will have a separate worship site
There will be one central place within one of the tribes
Each person may choose a place for himself
challenge.explanation: The verse points to one place chosen by the Lord, not many places chosen by tribes or individuals.

challenge.question: What detail about the offerings is easy to overlook in verses 11 and 14?
answers: Only burnt offerings may be brought
Vows need not be brought
The command includes everything the Lord commands, not only one type of offering
challenge.explanation: Verse 11 lists several kinds of offerings, and verse 14 summarizes them as everything the Lord commands.

questions.question: What is the central change between the situation “this day” and the future in the land?
answers: Instead of everyone doing as he pleases, worship will take place where the Lord chooses
Instead of worshiping the Lord, they will worship idols
Instead of rejoicing, the people will be forbidden to rejoice
questions.explanation: The present situation involves individual choice, while the future commands offerings at the place chosen by the Lord.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “the place which the Lord shall choose in one of thy tribes”?
answers: Each tribe will have a separate worship site
There will be one central place within one of the tribes
Each person may choose a place for himself
questions.explanation: The verse points to one place chosen by the Lord, not many places chosen by tribes or individuals.

questions.question: What detail about the offerings is easy to overlook in verses 11 and 14?
answers: Only burnt offerings may be brought
Vows need not be brought
The command includes everything the Lord commands, not only one type of offering
questions.explanation: Verse 11 lists several kinds of offerings, and verse 14 summarizes them as everything the Lord commands.

paragraphs.title: Eating Ordinary Meat and Holy Offerings

easy.question: What may a person eat in all his towns, according to verse 15?
answers: Meat
Blood
Tithes only
easy.explanation: The verse permits people to eat meat in all their towns, according to the Lord’s blessing.

easy.question: What may not be eaten according to verse 16?
answers: Meat
Blood
Grain
easy.explanation: The verse explicitly says, “Only ye shall not eat the blood.”

easy.question: Where must tithes and vows be eaten?
answers: In every home
Only in the wilderness
Before the Lord at the place He chooses
easy.explanation: Verse 18 commands that they be eaten before the Lord at the place He chooses.

medium.question: What is the main difference between ordinary meat and tithes and vows?
answers: Ordinary meat may be eaten in every town, while tithes and vows are eaten at the chosen place
Ordinary meat is forbidden, while tithes may be eaten anywhere
There is no difference between them
medium.explanation: Ordinary meat may be eaten locally, but holy offerings are eaten before the Lord at the chosen place.

medium.question: In “all thy vows which thou vowest,” what are “vows”?
answers: Foods that you cook
Promises or offerings dedicated to the Lord
Houses that you build
medium.explanation: Vows are commitments or offerings that a person promises to give to the Lord.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites commanded to rejoice before the Lord with the Levite?
answers: Because the Levite owned the land
Because the Levite prepared the meat
Because the Levite was to share in the joy of eating before the Lord
medium.explanation: The Levite is included among those who rejoice, and the next verse warns Israel not to forsake him.

challenge.question: Which conclusion correctly combines the permissions and prohibitions in these verses?
answers: Ordinary meat may be eaten in every town, but blood is always forbidden and holy offerings belong at the chosen place
All food must be eaten only at the chosen place
Blood may be eaten if it is served with tithes
challenge.explanation: The verses distinguish ordinary meat, forbidden blood, and holy offerings eaten before the Lord.

challenge.question: What can be understood from the contrast between “in all thy gates” and “at the place which the Lord shall choose”?
answers: All eating must take place at the temple
Private eating in local settlements differs from eating holy offerings at the central place
Eating inside towns is forbidden
challenge.explanation: The first phrase refers to local settlements, while the second refers to the special place of worship.

challenge.question: What point in verse 19 is easy to overlook?
answers: The warning is repeated only during festivals
The warning applies only to priests
The Levite must be remembered all the days Israel lives in the land
challenge.explanation: The verse says not to forsake the Levite as long as they live upon the earth, making this a continuing duty.

questions.question: Which conclusion correctly combines the permissions and prohibitions in these verses?
answers: Ordinary meat may be eaten in every town, but blood is always forbidden and holy offerings belong at the chosen place
All food must be eaten only at the chosen place
Blood may be eaten if it is served with tithes
questions.explanation: The verses distinguish ordinary meat, forbidden blood, and holy offerings eaten before the Lord.

questions.question: What can be understood from the contrast between “in all thy gates” and “at the place which the Lord shall choose”?
answers: All eating must take place at the temple
Private eating in local settlements differs from eating holy offerings at the central place
Eating inside towns is forbidden
questions.explanation: The first phrase refers to local settlements, while the second refers to the special place of worship.

questions.question: What point in verse 19 is easy to overlook?
answers: The warning is repeated only during festivals
The warning applies only to priests
The Levite must be remembered all the days Israel lives in the land
questions.explanation: The verse says not to forsake the Levite as long as they live upon the earth, making this a continuing duty.

paragraphs.title: Permission to Eat Meat Within the Land

easy.question: What may a person eat when he longs for meat?
answers: Meat
Only bread
Only fruit
easy.explanation: The verse says that a person who longs for meat may eat meat.

easy.question: What is forbidden to eat according to these verses?
answers: The meat
The blood
The grain
easy.explanation: The verses repeatedly emphasize that blood must not be eaten.

easy.question: What must be done with the blood?
answers: Keep it in a vessel
Drink it
Pour it on the ground
easy.explanation: Verse 24 says to pour it upon the earth as water.

medium.question: Why may people eat in their towns when the chosen place is far away?
answers: Because the distance makes it difficult to reach
Because meat may not be eaten at the chosen place
Because the towns are more holy
medium.explanation: When the chosen place is too far away, the Torah permits people to slaughter and eat in their towns.

medium.question: What does the comparison with the roebuck and the hart teach?
answers: Only priests may eat
The clean and unclean may eat together
Meat may not be eaten at home
medium.explanation: As with the roebuck and hart, both the clean and unclean may eat this meat alike.

medium.question: In “whatsoever thy soul lusteth after,” what does “lusteth after” mean?
answers: Desires or longs for
Fears
Commands
medium.explanation: The phrase refers to a person’s desire or longing to eat meat.

challenge.question: Why does the Torah connect the prohibition against eating blood with the fact that blood is life?
answers: To emphasize that blood is connected with the creature’s life and must be treated with respect
To teach that blood tastes especially good
To permit eating the blood of a roebuck only
challenge.explanation: The verse says that the blood is the life, so it must not be eaten with the flesh.

challenge.question: Which sequence agrees with the instructions in these verses?
answers: Eat the blood, then pour out the meat
Eat the meat and keep the blood
Do not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground
challenge.explanation: The verses forbid eating the blood and command that it be poured on the ground.

challenge.question: What practical and moral reason is given for obeying the prohibition against eating blood?
answers: So the meat will be more expensive
So it will go well with the person and his children when he does what is right before the Lord
So the person may eat only at the chosen place
challenge.explanation: Verse 25 says that obedience will bring good to the person and his children because he does what is right before the Lord.

questions.question: Why does the Torah connect the prohibition against eating blood with the fact that blood is life?
answers: To emphasize that blood is connected with the creature’s life and must be treated with respect
To teach that blood tastes especially good
To permit eating the blood of a roebuck only
questions.explanation: The verse says that the blood is the life, so it must not be eaten with the flesh.

questions.question: Which sequence agrees with the instructions in these verses?
answers: Eat the blood, then pour out the meat
Eat the meat and keep the blood
Do not eat the blood; pour it out on the ground
questions.explanation: The verses forbid eating the blood and command that it be poured on the ground.

questions.question: What practical and moral reason is given for obeying the prohibition against eating blood?
answers: So the meat will be more expensive
So it will go well with the person and his children when he does what is right before the Lord
So the person may eat only at the chosen place
questions.explanation: Verse 25 says that obedience will bring good to the person and his children because he does what is right before the Lord.

paragraphs.title: Bringing Holy Offerings and the Promise of Blessing

easy.question: What must be brought to the place the Lord chooses?
answers: Holy things and vows
All the people
Weapons of war
easy.explanation: The verse commands that holy things and vows be brought to the chosen place.

easy.question: Where must the blood of the sacrifices be poured?
answers: On the ground
On the altar of the Lord
Into a special vessel
easy.explanation: The verse says that the blood of the sacrifices shall be poured on the altar of the Lord.

easy.question: Who will benefit when the commands are observed and carried out?
answers: Only the priests
Only the wilderness generation
The person and his children after him
easy.explanation: The verse promises that it will go well with the person and his children after him.

medium.question: What sequence is described regarding vows and sacrifices?
answers: They are taken to the chosen place, offered, and then the meat is eaten
They are eaten at home and brought later
The blood is poured out and only afterward are vows made
medium.explanation: The holy things and vows are first brought to the chosen place, then the offerings are made and the meat is eaten.

medium.question: In “thy vows thou shalt take, and go,” what does “take” mean?
answers: Forget
Carry or bring with you
Sell
medium.explanation: In the context of going to the chosen place, “take” means to carry or bring the vows.

medium.question: What is the connection between doing what is good and right and the promise in the verse?
answers: Doing good means no offering will be needed
Doing good permits eating only the blood
Doing what is good and right is the reason it will go well with the person and his children
medium.explanation: The verse connects doing what is good and right with the promise of blessing.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “Only” at the beginning of verse 26?
answers: The holy things and vows must be carefully brought to the chosen place
Nothing may be brought to the chosen place
Only things unrelated to worship may be brought
challenge.explanation: “Only” highlights the holy things and vows that are to be taken to the place chosen by the Lord.

challenge.question: What does “Observe and hear” teach about obeying the command?
answers: It is enough to hear without obeying
The words must be carefully observed, heard, and carried out
The words must be kept secret
challenge.explanation: The command combines careful observance with hearing and responding; the verse then says, “when thou doest.”

challenge.question: What detail extends the effect of obedience beyond the individual?
answers: The altar is mentioned twice
The meat is eaten after the offering
The promise that his children after him will prosper forever
challenge.explanation: The promise includes not only the individual but also his children after him, “for ever.”

questions.question: What can be inferred from “Only” at the beginning of verse 26?
answers: The holy things and vows must be carefully brought to the chosen place
Nothing may be brought to the chosen place
Only things unrelated to worship may be brought
questions.explanation: “Only” highlights the holy things and vows that are to be taken to the place chosen by the Lord.

questions.question: What does “Observe and hear” teach about obeying the command?
answers: It is enough to hear without obeying
The words must be carefully observed, heard, and carried out
The words must be kept secret
questions.explanation: The command combines careful observance with hearing and responding; the verse then says, “when thou doest.”

questions.question: What detail extends the effect of obedience beyond the individual?
answers: The altar is mentioned twice
The meat is eaten after the offering
The promise that his children after him will prosper forever
questions.explanation: The promise includes not only the individual but also his children after him, “for ever.”

paragraphs.title: Warning Against Imitating the Nations’ Worship

easy.question: What will happen to the Israelites according to the verse?
answers: They will be driven from their land
They will inherit the land and dwell in it
They will return to Egypt
easy.explanation: The verse says that Israel will possess the land and dwell there.

easy.question: What does the Lord warn the Israelites against?
answers: Being drawn after the nations and their gods
Working their land
Entering the land
easy.explanation: The Lord warns them not to be ensnared by the nations or inquire after their gods.

easy.question: What must the Israelites not say according to the verse?
answers: How will we inherit the land?
When will we live in the land?
How did these nations serve their gods, so that we may do likewise?
easy.explanation: The verse warns them not to ask how the nations worshiped their gods in order to imitate them.

medium.question: What is the order of events described in verse 29?
answers: The nations will be destroyed, Israel will inherit the land, and then Israel will dwell there
Israel will dwell in the land, then arrive there, and afterward the nations will be destroyed
The nations will worship their gods, and Israel will return to Egypt
medium.explanation: First the Lord cuts off the nations, then Israel inherits the land and dwells there.

medium.question: In “that thou be not snared by following them,” what does “snared” mean?
answers: Learn their language
Be trapped or drawn after them
Build houses for them
medium.explanation: The word means to be trapped or drawn in; the context warns against adopting the nations’ worship.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites forbidden to inquire how the nations served their gods?
answers: Because such inquiry might lead them to imitate the nations
Because learning anything new is forbidden
Because the nations worshiped no gods
medium.explanation: The verse warns that wanting to know how the nations worshiped might lead Israel to do the same.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast between the two parts of these verses?
answers: War and peace
Inheriting the land and the danger of adopting the nations’ practices
Work and agriculture
challenge.explanation: The passage describes Israel’s inheritance of the land and immediately warns against following pagan worship.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “after that they be destroyed from before thee”?
answers: The danger of their influence remains even after they are defeated
The nations will continue to rule the land
Israel will remain in the wilderness
challenge.explanation: The warning applies even after the nations are gone, because their practices could still influence Israel.

challenge.question: Which word emphasizes that this warning requires special caution?
answers: Dwell
Possess
Take heed
challenge.explanation: “Take heed” is a strong command to be especially careful and begins the warning against following the nations.

questions.question: What is the central contrast between the two parts of these verses?
answers: War and peace
Inheriting the land and the danger of adopting the nations’ practices
Work and agriculture
questions.explanation: The passage describes Israel’s inheritance of the land and immediately warns against following pagan worship.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “after that they be destroyed from before thee”?
answers: The danger of their influence remains even after they are defeated
The nations will continue to rule the land
Israel will remain in the wilderness
questions.explanation: The warning applies even after the nations are gone, because their practices could still influence Israel.

questions.question: Which word emphasizes that this warning requires special caution?
answers: Dwell
Possess
Take heed
questions.explanation: “Take heed” is a strong command to be especially careful and begins the warning against following the nations.

paragraphs.title: The Prohibition of Idolatry and Abominable Practices

easy.question: To whom is “Thou shalt not do so” addressed?
answers: The people of Israel
The kings of the nations
The prophets only
easy.explanation: The verse commands the people of Israel not to do the practices described.

easy.question: What did those people do to their children?
answers: Sent them to school
Burned them in the fire
Hid them in the house
easy.explanation: The verse says that they burned their sons and daughters in the fire to their gods.

easy.question: Whom did those people worship?
answers: Their gods
Moses
The king of Israel
easy.explanation: The verse says that they performed these acts for their gods.

medium.question: Why were the Israelites forbidden to do the acts described in the verse?
answers: Because they were difficult to perform
Because they were military customs
Because they were an abomination hated by the Lord
medium.explanation: The verse explains that these acts were an abomination to the Lord, which He hates.

medium.question: What does “abomination” mean in “every abomination to the Lord”?
answers: A beloved act
A detestable and hated act
A secret act
medium.explanation: The following words, “which he hateth,” explain that an abomination is something detestable and hated by the Lord.

medium.question: What connection does the verse make between idolatry and burning children?
answers: Burning children was part of their idolatrous worship
Burning children was punishment for idolatry
There was no connection between the acts
medium.explanation: The verse says they burned their sons and daughters in the fire to their gods, presenting this as part of their worship.

challenge.question: What can be inferred from “Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God”?
answers: The Lord may be worshiped in any way, including forbidden acts
The Lord must not be worshiped by imitating the corrupt practices of idolaters
It is forbidden to speak about worshiping the Lord
challenge.explanation: The verse warns Israel not to direct toward the Lord practices associated with idolatry, especially detestable acts.

challenge.question: Which detail emphasizes that children of both sexes were harmed?
answers: “Thou shalt not do so”
“To their gods”
“Their sons and their daughters”
challenge.explanation: The verse specifically mentions both sons and daughters.

challenge.question: What is the central contrast in the verse?
answers: The Lord’s commands and an act that the Lord hates
Sons and daughters
Fire and water
challenge.explanation: The verse commands Israel not to imitate what the idolaters did because the Lord hates those acts.

questions.question: What can be inferred from “Thou shalt not do so unto the Lord thy God”?
answers: The Lord may be worshiped in any way, including forbidden acts
The Lord must not be worshiped by imitating the corrupt practices of idolaters
It is forbidden to speak about worshiping the Lord
questions.explanation: The verse warns Israel not to direct toward the Lord practices associated with idolatry, especially detestable acts.

questions.question: Which detail emphasizes that children of both sexes were harmed?
answers: “Thou shalt not do so”
“To their gods”
“Their sons and their daughters”
questions.explanation: The verse specifically mentions both sons and daughters.

questions.question: What is the central contrast in the verse?
answers: The Lord’s commands and an act that the Lord hates
Sons and daughters
Fire and water
questions.explanation: The verse commands Israel not to imitate what the idolaters did because the Lord hates those acts.
